partners.diseaseBName: non-spherocytic hemolytic anemia due to hexokinase deficiency
partners.mechanism_chain: BPGM (HGNC:1107) —DISRUPTS→ Glycolysis (Reactome:R-HSA-5693373); HK1 (HGNC:4907) —DISRUPTS→ Glycolysis (Reactome:R-HSA-5693373); Glycolysis (Reactome:R-HSA-5693373) —DECREASES→ ATP (CHEBI:15422); ATP (CHEBI:15422) —LEADS_TO→ Hemolytic anemia (HP:0001874); ATP (CHEBI:15422) —LEADS_TO→ Non-spherocytic hemolytic anemia (HP:0004805). Mutations in BPGM (diphosphoglycerate mutase) or HK1 (hexokinase 1) lead to deficiencies in their respective enzymes. Both enzymes are critical for glycolysis, the primary pathway for ATP production in red blood cells. Impaired glycolysis results in reduced ATP levels, which are essential for maintaining red blood cell shape and function, ultimately leading to hemolytic anemia.

partners.mechanism_chain: BPGM (HGNC:1139) —DISRUPTS→ 2,3-Bisphosphoglycerate (CHEBI:16778); 2,3-Bisphosphoglycerate (CHEBI:16778) —DECREASES→ Glycolysis (KEGG:00010); TPI1 (HGNC:11723) —DISRUPTS→ Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate (CHEBI:15505); Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate (CHEBI:15505) —DECREASES→ Glycolysis (KEGG:00010); Glycolysis (KEGG:00010) —DECREASES→ ATP (CHEBI:15422); Glycolysis (KEGG:00010) —LEADS_TO→ Hemolytic anemia (HP:0001874); ATP (CHEBI:15422) —DECREASES→ Neurological dysfunction (HP:0001257). Loss-of-function mutations in BPGM (causing hemolytic anemia) lead to decreased levels of 2,3-BPG, which affects oxygen release from hemoglobin. Simultaneously, loss-of-function mutations in TPI1 (causing neurological dysfunction and potentially contributing to anemia) impair a key step in glycolysis, leading to reduced ATP production and accumulation of upstream metabolites. Both pathways converge on impaired glycolysis and consequently reduced ATP production, impacting erythrocyte function and overall cellular energy homeostasis, which can manifest as hemolytic anemia and neurological symptoms.

partners.diseaseBName: glycogen storage disease due to phosphoglycerate mutase deficiency
partners.mechanism_chain: Phosphoglycerate Mutase 2 (HGNC:9138) —DECREASES→ 2,3-Bisphosphoglycerate (CHEBI:16874); 2,3-Bisphosphoglycerate (CHEBI:16874) —DISRUPTS→ Glycolysis / ATP Production (REACT:R-HSA-6959977); Glycolysis / ATP Production (REACT:R-HSA-6959977) —LEADS_TO→ Hemolytic Anemia (HP:0001874); Phosphoglycerate Mutase 2 (HGNC:9138) —DECREASES→ Glucose-6-phosphate (CHEBI:17307); Glucose-6-phosphate (CHEBI:17307) —LEADS_TO→ Glycogen Storage Disease (HP:0005910). Mutations in PGAM2 lead to a loss-of-function, resulting in decreased production of 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate, which is essential for regulating oxygen affinity in red blood cells, thereby causing hemolytic anemia. Concurrently, the same loss-of-function in PGAM2 impairs glycolysis by disrupting the conversion of 3-phosphoglycerate to 2-phosphoglycerate, leading to the accumulation of upstream metabolites like glucose-6-phosphate and consequent glycogen storage.

partners.mechanism_chain: BPGM (HGNC:1134) —DISRUPTS→ 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate (CHEBI:16157); 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate (CHEBI:16157) —DECREASES→ red blood cell glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-164577); red blood cell glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-164577) —DECREASES→ ATP (CHEBI:15378); red blood cell glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-164577) —LEADS_TO→ hemolytic anemia (HP:0001874); HK1 (HGNC:4873) —DECREASES→ ATP (CHEBI:15378); ATP (CHEBI:15378) —LEADS_TO→ Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (HP:0002485). This disruption leads to decreased ATP production within red blood cells, resulting in hemolytic anemia. The convergence lies in the shared consequence of impaired cellular ATP generation due to disruptions in glycolytic pathways, affecting distinct cell types (erythrocytes vs. neurons) but stemming from a common mechanistic theme of compromised energy homeostasis.

Mutations in BPGM (diphosphoglycerate mutase) or HK1 (hexokinase 1) lead to deficiencies in their respective enzymes. Both enzymes are critical for glycolysis, the primary pathway for ATP production in red blood cells. Impaired glycolysis results in reduced ATP levels, which are essential for maintaining red blood cell shape and function, ultimately leading to hemolytic anemia.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in BPGM or HK1 do not impair ATP production in erythrocytes, or that reduced ATP levels do not lead to red blood cell fragility and hemolysis. _(variant: None)_
